A static initializer runs during class initialization, before the class’s first relevant active use, not simply whenever a file is loaded.OOP07

Question 166

What is the output of the below given Java code? Assume every necessary components of the program are included. int i; for (i = 0; i < 5; i++) { if (i % 2 == 0) System.out.print ( i + " "); System.out.print ( i + 1); }

  • A. 0 12 34 5
  • B. None of the choices is correct
  • C. 0 2 4 6
  • D. 0 122 344 5

Source

  • Mock exam 2 · Question 15

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Trace condition tests, control transfers and printing as separate steps.

OOP-S02 · Java 17 floating-point evaluation and printed doubles

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

OOP25 · Control flow traces and exact printing

OOP-S02 · Java 17 floating-point evaluation and printed doubles

Correct answer: D — 0 122 344 5.

Only the first print is controlled by if. At i=0,2,4 it prints the even value followed by a space; every iteration then prints i+1 without a separator. The contributions are "0 1", "2", "2 3", "4", "4 5". Joining them produces "0 122 344 5", exactly as OOP25 records.

Evidence in the complete study note

Count executions independently from printing. For i=0..4, if(i%2==0) print(i+" "); followed unconditionally by print(i+1); produces "0 122 344 5".OOP25
A print call emits its value without inserting a separator or ending the line. A println call emits its value followed by a line terminator. Spaces must come from the supplied text or explicit output operations; adjacent calls do not automatically separate their values.OOP-S02

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — This omits digits from the unconditional i+1 prints on odd and even iterations.

B · incorrect — D supplies the exact concatenated output, so none of the choices is false.

C · incorrect — The unconditional print runs five times; the output is not just an even-number sequence.

D · correct — Joining every conditional and unconditional print yields the exact string 0 122 344 5.

Question 168

Which Java member access modifier permits subclasses in other packages to access inherited members through their own inherited context, while excluding unrelated clients in those other packages? Same-package access is allowed.

  • A. protected
  • B. private
  • C. default
  • D. public

Adapted from

  • MOE Computer Science Exit Exam · Question 3-4

  • National Computer Science Exit Exam · Question 63

  • National Computer Science Exit Exam · Question 66

  • National Computer Science Exit Exam

  • MOE Computer Science Exit Exam

  • Computer Science Exit Exam practice collection · Question 97

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Locate the accessing code, declaring type, package and receiver before applying visibility rules.

Study-guide sections

OOP08 · Access control and package boundaries

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

OOP08 · Access control and package boundaries

Correct answer: A — protected

protected includes same-package access and also permits qualified subclass access across packages. That matches the revised boundary, which excludes unrelated clients in other packages while allowing same-package clients. private does not generally expose inherited members to separately declared subclasses, package access does not reach other packages, and public allows unrelated external clients. The question no longer demands an impossible universal subclasses-only rule.

Evidence in the complete study note

For ordinary members: private restricts access to the declaring class/nest; no modifier grants package access; protected grants same-package access plus qualified subclass access; public is widest, provided the declaring type itself is accessible.OOP08
Across packages, a subclass accessing a protected instance member must do so through its own inherited context or an appropriate subclass-typed receiver, not any arbitrary superclass object. protected therefore does not mean “subclasses only”: unrelated classes in the same package also have access.OOP08

Choice by choice

A · correct — protected provides same-package access plus the specified qualified cross-package subclass access.

B · incorrect — private does not grant the requested general cross-package subclass access.

C · incorrect — Package/default access does not extend to subclasses in another package.

D · incorrect — public also permits unrelated accessible external clients, violating the boundary.

Correct answer: D — String m = new String("Exit Exam");

A String literal uses double quotes, while a character literal supplies one char in single quotes.   • C. To define a blueprint of a class
  • D. To achieve multiple inheritance

OOP20 · Conflicting interface methods and abstract class choice

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

OOP19 · Interfaces: contracts and modern Java

OOP02 · Four principles and the difference between hiding and abstraction

OOP20 · Conflicting interface methods and abstract class choice

Correct answers (select all): A, B, D — To define a blueprint for a class; To allow multiple inheritance; To hide internal implementation details

An interface specifies an operation contract that implementing classes satisfy, so the qualified blueprint description is valid. A class can implement multiple interfaces, gaining multiple type inheritance. Clients can use the contract without depending on a particular implementation’s internals, supporting abstraction. Interfaces are not directly instantiated, so creating objects directly is not their purpose. The multi-select form therefore accepts A, B and D.

Evidence in the complete study note

interface Payable{double getPaymentAmount();} declares an abstract public operation. class Invoice implements Payable must provide public double getPaymentAmount(), perhaps returning getQuantity()*getPricePerItem().OOP19
Information hiding keeps implementation decisions behind a stable interface. Abstraction presents the essential operations while omitting details irrelevant to the caller.OOP02
Use an abstract class for shared state, construction and common implementation; use an interface for a capability across unrelated classes and multiple type inheritance.OOP20

Choice by choice

A · correct — An operation blueprint is the contract that implementations must satisfy.

B · correct — Implementing multiple interfaces supports multiple type inheritance.

C · incorrect — An interface cannot be instantiated directly.

D · correct — The public contract lets callers use capabilities without depending on internal implementation details.

Alternative version 1

Correct answers (select all): C, D — Interfaces define capability contracts and support multiple type inheritance.

This variant places the contract/blueprint purpose at C and multiple type inheritance at D. Both are valid: implementing objects satisfy the public operation contract, and a class may implement several interfaces. Interfaces have no constructors or per-instance fields, so they do not create class constructors or define an object’s complete state and implementation. Its selected labels therefore differ from the primary option set.

interface Payable{double getPaymentAmount();} declares an abstract public operation. class Invoice implements Payable must provide public double getPaymentAmount(), perhaps returning getQuantity()*getPricePerItem(). A class can extend a superclass and implement zero or more interfaces. An interface can extend several interfaces. No interface instance fields or constructors exist; fields are implicitly public static final.OOP19

Use an abstract class for shared state, construction and common implementation; use an interface for a capability across unrelated classes and multiple type inheritance.OOP20

A · incorrect — Interfaces have no constructors, so creating multiple constructors is not their purpose.

B · incorrect — An interface specifies capabilities rather than complete per-instance state and implementation.

C · correct — The defined blueprint is an operation contract for implementing classes.

D · correct — Several interface types provide multiple type inheritance.

Correct answer: C — Inheritance, specifically multiple interface/type inheritance.

Implementing several interfaces gives the class several interface types and forms multiple type inheritance. Inheritance is therefore the relationship concept requested. B · incorrect — Encapsulation groups state and controls access rather than forming the specified type relationship.

C · correct — The class acquires multiple interface types, which is multiple type inheritance.

D · incorrect — Interface is the construct defining a contract, not the requested relationship concept.

An interface cannot be instantiated directly without an implementation. An interface reference can instead hold an implementing object and invoke its contract methods. Question 183

Which statement is wrong about a Java try-catch construct? Assume any exception considered has a matching catch, and no earlier control transfer prevents reaching it.

  • A. The execution control is moved to catch block after exception occur in try block
  • B. When exception occurs, the execution of try block is interrupted
  • C. The catch block is executed once regardless of exceptions in try block
  • D. The catch block is used to handle exceptions that occur in try block

Adapted from

  • Computer Science model exam collection · Question 24

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Check the thrown type and catch order before tracing propagation or handler output.

Study-guide sections

OOP30 · throw, throws and catch selection

OOP31 · finally, cleanup and diagnostic information

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

OOP30 · throw, throws and catch selection

OOP31 · finally, cleanup and diagnostic information

Correct answer: C — The catch block is executed once regardless of exceptions in try block

If the try block completes normally, its catch does not execute. If an exception occurs, normal execution of the try is interrupted and the matching handler runs. Thus the claim that catch runs once regardless of exceptions is false. Catch is conditional handling, whereas finally normally provides cleanup after the try and any selected handler. The matching-handler assumption makes the other transfer statements precise.

Evidence in the complete study note

try encloses guarded operations; a matching catch handles the thrown type or a subtype. Execution skips the remainder of the try when a throw occurs.OOP30
finally normally executes after try and any selected catch, including when leaving by return or propagating an exception.OOP31

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — With the stated matching-handler assumption, an exception transfers control to that catch.

B · incorrect — The exception interrupts normal execution and skips the remaining try body.

C · correct — This is false: normal completion of try does not execute catch.

D · incorrect — The matching catch handles the exception thrown during try.

An accessible abstract Class_A declares public abstract String welcome(); and has an accessible no-argument constructor. Which independent concrete definition of Class_B compiles?   • B. public class Class_B extends Class_A { public int welcome() { int x = 10; return x; } }
  • C. public class Class_B extends Class_A { public String whatObjectAmI() { return "I am a class D object"; } public String welcome() { return "I am a class C object"; } public int welcome(int y) { int x = 2 * y; return x; } }
  • D. public class Class_B extends Class_A { public void welcome(String str) { } }

Correct answer: C — public class Class_B extends Class_A { public String whatObjectAmI() { return "I am a class D object"; } public String welcome() { return "I am a class C object"; } public int welcome(int y) { int x = 2 * y; return x; } }

The required inherited method has no parameters and returns String. C supplies that exact public implementation and may additionally overload welcome with an int parameter. A has no welcome implementation, B returns an incompatible int, and D supplies only a different-parameter overload. Those concrete subclasses leave the abstract contract unsatisfied or violate return compatibility.

A concrete subclass must provide or inherit implementations of all required abstract methods; otherwise it must itself be abstract. If parent declares abstract String welcome(), a String welcome() implementation is required; int welcome() is incompatible, and welcome(int) merely adds an overload. Overloaded methods share a name but have different parameter types, counts or type order. Return type alone is insufficient in Java and C++.OOP12

Choice by choice

B · incorrect — int is incompatible with the required String return for the same signature.

D · incorrect — welcome(String) is an overload and does not implement no-argument welcome().

Alternative version 1

Inside an instance method declared in the current subclass, which descriptions correctly identify the parent-class context selected by Java super? Select all that apply.

  • A. It refers to the current object instance.
  • B. It refers to the superclass of the current class.

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

OOP16 · this, super, fields and static hiding

OOP13 · Inheritance and useful relationships

Correct answer: A — To access the superclass of a derived class.

super selects the superclass context for member access and can request a superclass implementation. A hidden parent field can be selected with super.name, and super.sound() directly calls the parent version. It does not allocate a separate parent object or name the current instance; this is the current-object reference. Method definitions use declarations, so A is the valid purpose among the primary choices.

Evidence in the complete study note

Java this denotes the current object; this.name=name distinguishes a field from a parameter. super.name selects a hidden superclass field; super.sound() directly requests the parent implementation. It does not create a second parent object. An unqualified instance call may dispatch dynamically; an explicit super call is different.OOP16
class Dog extends Animal declares a subclass/derived/child of a superclass/base/parent.OOP13

Choice by choice

A · correct — This describes selecting the superclass context and its members.

D · incorrect — A method declaration defines a method; super does not do that.

Alternative version 1

Correct answers (select all): B, D — Both B and D describe the superclass context selected by super.

The superclass of the current class and the class from which the current class derives name the same parent relationship, so B and D both apply. super selects that parent context for member access or explicit parent implementation calls. A instead describes this, while C identifies the current subclass containing the declared method. The variant therefore needs multiple selection even though the primary choices have one correct answer.

Java this denotes the current object; this.name=name distinguishes a field from a parameter. super.name selects a hidden superclass field; super.sound() directly requests the parent implementation. It does not create a second parent object. An unqualified instance call may dispatch dynamically; an explicit super call is different.OOP16

class Dog extends Animal declares a subclass/derived/child of a superclass/base/parent.OOP13

A · incorrect — The current object instance is denoted by this, not the parent-context selector super.

B · correct — The superclass is the parent context selected by super.

C · incorrect — The method is declared in the current subclass, whereas super selects its parent context.

D · correct — The class from which the current class derives is its superclass, equivalent to B.

Study-guide references

OOP18 · Abstract classes and concrete implementations

OOP07 · Static members, static blocks and final

Correct answer: D — Interfaces can extend multiple interfaces; an abstract class instead implements interfaces and extends one class.

OOP19 permits an interface to extend several interfaces and a class to extend one superclass while implementing multiple interfaces. Thus D is correct when extend retains its Java declaration meaning. It must not be paraphrased as abstract classes cannot implement multiple interfaces. A is outdated for modern interfaces, B wrongly excludes class static methods, and C wrongly permits abstract instantiation.

A class can extend a superclass and implement zero or more interfaces. An interface can extend several interfaces.OOP19
A method declaration without private, default or static is implicitly public abstract. Modern interfaces may also have default/static method bodies, and Java 9+ private helper methods.OOP19
An abstract class cannot be directly instantiated but can define fields, constructors, abstract methods and concrete methods.OOP18
static gives one field per loaded class, shared by its instances. If count starts at zero and every constructor increments it, three creations leave count=3. Prefer ClassName.count and ClassName.utility().OOP07

B · incorrect — Abstract classes can have static methods; their abstract modifier does not prohibit class-level methods.

C · incorrect — An abstract class cannot be directly instantiated, so the first half of this distinction is false.

D · correct — An interface extends multiple interfaces; a class implements them instead and has one direct superclass.

Question 201

What is the output of the following Java code snippet? class MyClass { public static void main(String[] args) { int x = 5; System.out.println(x++); System.out.println(++x); } }

  • B. 5, 7
  • C. 6, 6

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

OOP-S02 · Java 17 floating-point evaluation and printed doubles

Correct answer: B — 5, then 7, on separate lines.

OOP24 gives this exact sequence: postfix x++ supplies the old value 5 and then stores 6; prefix ++x then stores and supplies 7. The two println calls print those values on separate lines. The commas in the choices describe the sequence rather than literal commas emitted by the program.

Evidence in the complete study note

Starting x=5, printing x++ then ++x gives 5 then 7.OOP24

D · incorrect — The second value is 7, but the first remains 5 because its increment is postfix.

Question 202

Which Java keyword directly exits the enclosing loop prematurely while allowing execution to continue after that loop in the same method?

  • A. break
  • B. continue
  • C. return
  • D. exit

Adapted from

  • Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 315

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Trace condition tests, control transfers and printing as separate steps.

Study-guide sections

OOP25 · Control flow traces and exact printing

OOP-S03 · Expression results, assignment and control headers

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

OOP25 · Control flow traces and exact printing

OOP-S03 · Expression results, assignment and control headers

Correct answer: A — break

break exits the enclosing loop and transfers control to the statement after it. continue skips the remaining body of the current iteration and may begin another iteration. return leaves the entire method, so it does not satisfy the stated requirement to continue after the loop in that same method. exit is not a Java loop-control keyword. The narrower control-flow target makes break unique.

Evidence in the complete study note

break exits the loop; continue skips its remaining body and then runs a for update.OOP25
An unlabeled break leaves the innermost enclosing loop or switch. continue moves to the next iteration step, while return leaves the current method and may supply a return value. These transfers have different destinations; return is not merely a loop exit.OOP-S03

Choice by choice

A · correct — break exits the loop and resumes after it within the method.

B · incorrect — continue proceeds toward another iteration rather than exiting the loop.

C · incorrect — return exits the entire method, contrary to the required continuation.

D · incorrect — exit is not a Java loop-control keyword.

Correct answer: C — It allows a variable or method to be accessed without creating an instance of the class.

Static members belong to the class, and the static method is accessible by class name without an object. Visibility and immutability are separate properties.

Evidence in the complete study note

static gives one field per loaded class, shared by its instances. If count starts at zero and every constructor increments it, three creations leave count=3. Prefer ClassName.count and ClassName.utility(). A static method has no current instance, but can still use instance members through an explicit object reference.OOP07
final prevents reassignment of a variable, overriding of a method or extension of a class.OOP07
For ordinary members: private restricts access to the declaring class/nest; no modifier grants package access; protected grants same-package access plus qualified subclass access; public is widest, provided the declaring type itself is accessible.OOP08

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Class membership does not mean belonging to the superclass

B · incorrect — Private is the visibility restriction

C · correct — Matches class access without creating an instance

D · incorrect — final, not static, prevents modification

Question 208

What is the output of the following Java code snippet? class MyClass { public static void main(String[] args) { String text = "Hello"; text += " World"; System.out.println(text); } }

  • A. Hello
  • B. World
  • C. Hello World
  • D. Compile error

Source

  • Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 321

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Separate identity, content equality, immutable values and references that may be reassigned.

Study-guide sections

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

OOP22 · Identity, equals, toString and immutable strings

OOP24 · Increment order and the character-space trap

Correct answer: C — Hello World.

OOP22 directly explains that text += " World" assigns a reference to a new concatenated result rather than mutating the original String. The variable therefore refers to "Hello World" before printing. String immutability does not prevent rebinding a non-final variable, so the code is valid and prints the combined text with its space.

Evidence in the complete study note

Java String objects are immutable. text += " World" assigns a reference to a new concatenated result and can print Hello World without mutating the original String object. final class String prevents subclassing; final alone does not make arbitrary objects immutable.OOP22
Once a String operand is encountered, + concatenates in left-to-right groups: 1+2+"x" gives "3x", while "x"+1+2 gives "x12".OOP24

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — The variable is rebound to the concatenated result, so it no longer prints only its initial text.

B · incorrect — Concatenation retains Hello and appends the space and World; it does not replace the entire content with World.

C · correct — The new concatenated String contains Hello, a space and World, and text refers to that result.

D · incorrect — String immutability permits this reference reassignment; the code does not attempt to mutate the original String.

Question 211

What is the purpose of the toString() method in Java?

  • A. To convert an object to a string representation.
  • B. To compare two objects for equality.
  • C. To perform arithmetic calculations.
  • D. To access the superclass methods.

Source

  • Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 324

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Separate identity, content equality, immutable values and references that may be reassigned.

Study-guide sections

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

OOP22 · Identity, equals, toString and immutable strings

OOP16 · this, super, fields and static hiding

Correct answer: A — Return an object’s textual representation.

OOP22 defines toString as giving a textual representation and distinguishes it from an equality test. A states that purpose. Comparing objects is the role of equals under the class’s policy, while arithmetic and superclass method access are separate operations. The representation need not create a new copy of the original object.

Evidence in the complete study note

For object references, == tests identity; equals invokes the class’s equality policy. Object.equals uses identity unless overridden; String.equals compares character content. Equal objects must have equal hashCode values when that contract is implemented. toString gives a textual representation, not an equality test.OOP22
super.name selects a hidden superclass field; super.sound() directly requests the parent implementation.OOP16

Choice by choice

A · correct — A textual String representation of an object is the purpose explicitly assigned to toString in OOP22.

B · incorrect — Object equality is handled by equals under the class’s equality policy, not by toString.

C · incorrect — Arithmetic calculations are not the defining contract of an object’s textual representation method.

D · incorrect — Superclass access uses super; it is not the purpose of toString.

Question 217

Assume an accessible inherited instance method is non-final, the subclass supplies the same name and parameter list with a compatible return type, and visibility is not reduced. Which descriptions fit the resulting method overriding? Select all that apply.

  • A. Creating multiple methods with the same name but different return types.
  • B. Creating multiple methods with the same name but different parameter lists.
  • C. Creating a new method with the same name and parameter list in the subclass.
  • D. Redefining a method in the subclass that already exists in the superclass.

Adapted from

  • Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 331

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

OOP14 · Overriding and restrictions

OOP12 · Method overloading and compile-time selection

Correct answers (select all): C, D — Creating a new method with the same name and parameter list in the subclass.; Redefining a method in the subclass that already exists in the superclass.

Under the stated eligibility, signature, return and visibility conditions, the subclass method overrides the inherited method. C describes the same name and parameters, and D describes redefining the inherited superclass operation, so both describe this case. Different parameter lists denote overloading instead. Merely changing return types does not define overriding or a valid overload. The assumptions make the two overlapping valid descriptions explicit.

Evidence in the complete study note

A subclass overrides an eligible inherited instance method with the same signature and a compatible return type; a covariant reference return may be a subtype. Visibility cannot become more restrictive, and checked exceptions cannot be broadened incompatibly.OOP14
Overloaded methods share a name but have different parameter types, counts or type order. Return type alone is insufficient in Java and C++.OOP12

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Different return types alone do not define overriding or distinguish valid overloads.

B · incorrect — Different parameter lists describe overloading rather than this same-signature override.

C · correct — The same-name, same-parameter subclass declaration is an override under the supplied conditions.

D · correct — It redefines the eligible inherited superclass operation under the supplied conditions.

Question 224

Which Java annotation requests compiler checking that a method overrides or implements an inherited method contract?

  • A. super
  • B. extends
  • C. implements
  • D. @Override

  • Computer Science MCQ practice collection · Question 339

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

OOP14 · Overriding and restrictions

OOP13 · Inheritance and useful relationships

OOP16 · this, super, fields and static hiding

Correct answer: D — @Override

@Override asks the compiler to verify that a declaration satisfies overriding rules. Java does not have an override keyword, and the annotation does not create an override by itself; the declaration must still meet the inherited-contract conditions. super selects parent context, extends declares class inheritance, and implements declares interface relationships. Correcting the requested construct to an annotation preserves the intended override-checking concept.

Evidence in the complete study note

A subclass overrides an eligible inherited instance method with the same signature and a compatible return type; a covariant reference return may be a subtype. Visibility cannot become more restrictive, and checked exceptions cannot be broadened incompatibly. @Override requests compiler checking; Java has no override keyword. Constructors, final methods, static methods and private parent methods are not overridden.OOP14
class Dog extends Animal declares a subclass/derived/child of a superclass/base/parent. A class extends one direct class and can implement multiple interfaces.OOP13
super.name selects a hidden superclass field; super.sound() directly requests the parent implementation.OOP16

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — super selects parent members or construction rather than checking a declaration’s override status.

B · incorrect — extends establishes class inheritance rather than annotating a method.

C · incorrect — implements establishes an interface relationship rather than checking one method declaration.

D · correct — @Override requests compiler verification of the overriding/implementation relationship.

Which purposes apply to Java interfaces? “Blueprint” means an operation contract, “state and behavior” in B means complete per-instance state and implementation, and “multiple inheritance” means type inheritance. Select all that apply.

Study-guide references

OOP19 · Interfaces: contracts and modern Java

Correct answers (select all): C, D — To define a blueprint of a class; To achieve multiple inheritance

An interface gives implementing classes an operation contract, so the defined blueprint purpose is valid. A class can implement multiple interfaces, supporting multiple type inheritance. Use an abstract class for shared state, construction and common implementation; use an interface for a capability across unrelated classes and multiple type inheritance.OOP20

Question 231

Consider this C++17 class and statements inside a valid main function: struct Meter { int reading = 0; void set(int reading) { this->reading = reading; } static int twice(int x) { return 2 * x; } }; Meter first, second; first.set(4); second.set(9); int doubled = Meter::twice(3); Which statement correctly describes the implicit object context during second.set(9) and the call to twice?

  • A. In set, this points to second; twice has no this pointer.
  • B. In set, this points to first; twice has no this pointer.
  • C. In set, this points to second; twice reuses second as its implicit object.
  • D. The hidden object argument is passed to the reading data member rather than to set.

Adapted from

  • Computer Science Exit Exam · 2018 · Question 9

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Use the stated language rules and identify whether a member call has an implicit current object.

Study-guide sections

OOP17 · C++ this and language-specific assumptions

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

OOP17 · C++ this and language-specific assumptions

Correct answer: A — In set, this points to second; twice has no this pointer.

Each non-static set call has an implicit object: first for first.set(4) and second for second.set(9). During the latter call, this therefore points to second, and this->reading selects that object’s field. The static twice function has no current object or this pointer, regardless of which instance method ran most recently. Data members themselves do not receive hidden call arguments.

Evidence in the complete study note

In ordinary C++17 non-static member functions, this is a pointer to the object on which the function is called; this->field selects a member. It is often explained as an implicit object argument to a member function call. It is not an argument passed to member variables, and a static member function has no this pointer.OOP17

Choice by choice

A · correct — second is the receiver of second.set(9); the static twice call has no implicit object.

B · incorrect — The earlier call on first does not make first the receiver of the later call on second.

C · incorrect — twice is static and does not acquire a this pointer from the most recent instance call.

D · incorrect — The implicit object belongs to the non-static function call; the reading data member does not receive a hidden argument.

Question 232

What will be the output of the following program segment? public class Calculation { public static void main(String[] args) { int sum = 0; for(int j = 1; j<=10; j++) { sum = sum + j; } System.out.println(+sum); }

  • A. 55
  • B. 44
  • C. 33
  • D. 66

Source

  • Computer Science Exit Exam · 2018 · Question 17

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

OOP25 · Control flow traces and exact printing

OOP-S03 · Expression results, assignment and control headers

Correct answer: A — 55 for the shown program segment.

The shown program segment initializes sum to zero and adds j for all values 1 through 10 inclusive. Its numerical result is 55. The unary plus in println(+sum) preserves that value. This is a program segment; a complete compilation unit also requires the outer class’s closing brace.

Evidence in the complete study note

Count executions independently from printing.OOP25
A loop summing j=1..10 yields 55.OOP25
Prefix ++ and -- update a variable before supplying its value; postfix forms supply the old value before the update. Multiplication, division and remainder bind before addition and subtraction; same-level binary arithmetic groups left to right. Integer division truncates toward zero. Unary plus preserves its numeric operand’s value.OOP-S03

Choice by choice

A · correct — The ten inclusive additions produce 55; unary plus leaves that integer unchanged.

B · incorrect — 44 is not the sum of the stated inclusive sequence 1 through 10.

C · incorrect — 33 does not match all ten additions performed by the shown loop.

D · incorrect — 66 would correspond to including an additional 11, which this condition excludes.

Question 235

A member declared in package p must be usable by an unrelated helper in p and by a subclass in package q through its inherited context. Unrelated classes outside p must be excluded. Which access category fits these requirements?

  • A. Public
  • B. Default
  • C. Private
  • D. Protected

  • Computer Science Exit Exam · 2018 · Question 69

Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

Locate the accessing code, declaring type, package and receiver before applying visibility rules.

Study-guide sections

OOP08 · Access control and package boundaries

Answer & Detailed Explanation

Study-guide references

OOP08 · Access control and package boundaries

Correct answer: D — Protected, with qualified subclass access across packages.

Protected permits same-package access, including an unrelated helper, and qualified subclass access from another package. It does not grant access to unrelated clients in other packages. Public violates that exclusion, package/default access cannot reach the other-package subclass, and private cannot admit the unrelated same-package helper. For an instance member, the cross-package receiver restriction remains part of the protected rule.

Evidence in the complete study note

For ordinary members: private restricts access to the declaring class/nest; no modifier grants package access; protected grants same-package access plus qualified subclass access; public is widest, provided the declaring type itself is accessible.OOP08
Across packages, a subclass accessing a protected instance member must do so through its own inherited context or an appropriate subclass-typed receiver, not any arbitrary superclass object. protected therefore does not mean “subclasses only”: unrelated classes in the same package also have access.OOP08

Choice by choice

A · incorrect — Public would also admit the unrelated other-package clients that the stem excludes.

B · incorrect — Default/package access would exclude the subclass in q.

C · incorrect — Private would exclude the unrelated helper in p.

D · correct — Protected provides both requested contexts while retaining the stated other-package exclusion.

            Question 242

            Under Java 17, what is the key restriction on an explicit this(...) invocation inside a constructor?

              Adapted from

              • Object-Oriented Programming review questions · Question 6

              Trace constructor delegation and initialization in the specified Java version.

              Study-guide sections

              OOP10 · Constructor chaining and initialization order

              Answer & Detailed Explanation

              Study-guide references

              OOP10 · Constructor chaining and initialization order

              Answer: It must be the first constructor statement and delegates to another constructor in the same class.

              Under Java 17, an explicit this(...) invocation must be the first constructor statement and delegates to another constructor of the same class. The constructor cannot also explicitly invoke super(...); the delegation chain reaches superclass construction through another constructor. The version qualification matters because later Java versions permit a restricted prologue, so the Java 17 rule should not be presented as timeless.

              Evidence in the complete study note

              Under Java 17 rules, an explicit this(args) or super(args) invocation must be the first constructor statement. this invokes another constructor in the same class; super invokes the immediate superclass constructor. A constructor cannot explicitly invoke both. If there is no explicit delegation, an implicit super() is inserted; a matching accessible no-argument parent constructor must exist.OOP10
              Java 25 permits restricted statements before explicit constructor invocation; the older first-statement rule must be version qualified.OOP10

                  Answer: Package-private/default access: omit an access modifier.

                  OOP08 says an ordinary member with no access modifier grants package access. This admits other code in the same package but does not admit an other-package subclass merely through inheritance. protected would be broader because it adds qualified cross-package subclass access; private would be narrower. The answer is omission, not a default keyword modifier.

                  Evidence in the complete study note

                  For ordinary members: private restricts access to the declaring class/nest; no modifier grants package access; protected grants same-package access plus qualified subclass access; public is widest, provided the declaring type itself is accessible.OOP08
                  Across packages, a subclass accessing a protected instance member must do so through its own inherited context or an appropriate subclass-typed receiver, not any arbitrary superclass object. protected therefore does not mean “subclasses only”: unrelated classes in the same package also have access.OOP08

                        Answer: Compilation fails: a Java class cannot extend two direct superclasses.

                        Question 248

                          Answer: The child declaration is independent; it does not override the private parent method.

                                Question 252

                                  Question 253

                                  Can an abstract class have a constructor? Can it be instantiated?

                                    Source

                                    • Object-Oriented Programming review questions · Question 17

                                    Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

                                    Check whether a class is concrete and whether every inherited abstract contract has an implementation.

                                    Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                    Study-guide references

                                    OOP18 · Abstract classes and concrete implementations

                                    OOP10 · Constructor chaining and initialization order

                                    Answer: Yes, it can have constructors; no, it cannot be directly instantiated.

                                    OOP18 allows an abstract class to define constructors alongside fields and concrete/abstract methods. Its constructor participates in initializing the inherited part of a concrete subclass object. That initialization role does not permit new of the abstract class itself. Direct instantiation remains prohibited even if the abstract class happens to contain no abstract methods.

                                      Answer: extends forms a single superclass relationship; implements fulfills one or more interface contracts.

It can also implement multiple interfaces, satisfying their required public operations through provided or inherited methods.                                             Question 258

                                                              Question 267

                                                              What is the difference between throw and throws in Java?

                                                                Source

                                                                • Object-Oriented Programming review questions · Question 31

                                                                Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

                                                                Check the thrown type and catch order before tracing propagation or handler output.

                                                                Study-guide sections

                                                                OOP30 · throw, throws and catch selection

                                                                Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                                Study-guide references

                                                                OOP30 · throw, throws and catch selection

                                                                Answer: throw actively raises an exception value; throws declares a method’s possible checked-exception obligation.

                                                                OOP30 contrasts throw new IOException("message") with throws IOException in a method signature. The first performs an action in control flow, skipping the remaining try body; the second declares an obligation that callers must handle or propagate. A throws clause does not itself throw anything, and throwing a checked exception still requires handling or declaration.

                                                                Evidence in the complete study note

                                                                throw new IOException("message") actively throws a value; throws IOException in a signature declares a possible checked exception. A caller must handle or propagate checked obligations. try encloses guarded operations; a matching catch handles the thrown type or a subtype. Execution skips the remainder of the try when a throw occurs.OOP30

                                                                Question 268

                                                                What happens if an exception occurs in a try block and there is no matching catch block?

                                                                  Source

                                                                  • Object-Oriented Programming review questions · Question 32

                                                                  Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

                                                                  Check the thrown type and catch order before tracing propagation or handler output.

                                                                  Study-guide sections

                                                                  OOP30 · throw, throws and catch selection

                                                                  OOP31 · finally, cleanup and diagnostic information

                                                                  Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                                  Study-guide references

                                                                  OOP30 · throw, throws and catch selection

                                                                  OOP31 · finally, cleanup and diagnostic information

                                                                  Answer: It propagates outward to a matching enclosing handler; if uncaught, its thread terminates.

                                                                  Without a matching local catch, the exception is not ignored and execution does not resume with the next ordinary statement in the try. OOP30 sends it outward through enclosing calls/handlers. Relevant finally blocks normally execute during that exit under OOP31’s limits. If no handler catches it, the uncaught exception terminates its thread, not necessarily every JVM thread.

                                                                  Evidence in the complete study note

                                                                  Execution skips the remainder of the try when a throw occurs.OOP30
                                                                  If no catch matches, the exception propagates outward and an uncaught exception terminates its thread.OOP30
                                                                  finally normally executes after try and any selected catch, including when leaving by return or propagating an exception. It is not guaranteed if the process/JVM exits or crashes, or control never leaves the try.OOP31

                                                                  Question 269

                                                                  Is it mandatory to handle an ArithmeticException?

                                                                    Source

                                                                    • Object-Oriented Programming review questions · Question 33

                                                                    Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

                                                                    Separate source errors from runtime exceptions and determine the hierarchy and checked obligation.

                                                                    Study-guide sections

                                                                    OOP29 · Exception hierarchy and checked obligations

                                                                    OOP30 · throw, throws and catch selection

                                                                    Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                                    Study-guide references

                                                                    OOP29 · Exception hierarchy and checked obligations

                                                                    OOP30 · throw, throws and catch selection

                                                                    Answer: No catch-or-declare obligation applies: ArithmeticException is unchecked.

                                                                    OOP29 lists ArithmeticException among unchecked exceptions, so Java does not require a surrounding catch or throws declaration merely because it may occur. A program can still catch it when that provides useful recovery. Unchecked means no mandatory compile-time handling obligation, not harmless behavior: an uncaught occurrence propagates and may terminate its thread.

                                                                    Evidence in the complete study note

                                                                    RuntimeException and Error subclasses are unchecked; other throwable classes are checked. IOException, FileNotFoundException and SQLException are standard checked examples. ArithmeticException, NullPointerException, ClassCastException and array bounds exceptions are unchecked.OOP29
                                                                    Checked does not mean the exception occurs at compile time: the compiler checks an obligation to catch or declare it, while an actual throw occurs at runtime.OOP29
                                                                    If no catch matches, the exception propagates outward and an uncaught exception terminates its thread.OOP30

                                                                    Question 270

                                                                    What is the order of execution in: try { ... } catch(E e) { ... } finally { ... }?

                                                                      Source

                                                                      • Object-Oriented Programming review questions · Question 34

                                                                      Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

                                                                      Check the thrown type and catch order before tracing propagation or handler output.

                                                                      Study-guide sections

                                                                      OOP30 · throw, throws and catch selection

                                                                      OOP31 · finally, cleanup and diagnostic information

                                                                      Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                                      Study-guide references

                                                                      OOP30 · throw, throws and catch selection

                                                                      OOP31 · finally, cleanup and diagnostic information

                                                                      Answer: Run try, then a matching catch if thrown, then normally finally.

                                                                      If try completes normally, no catch executes and finally follows. If an exception is thrown, the remaining try body is skipped, a matching catch runs if available, and finally normally executes before continuation or outward propagation. finally also normally runs on return. Process/JVM exit, a crash or control never leaving try prevents an unconditional always claim.

                                                                      Evidence in the complete study note

                                                                      Execution skips the remainder of the try when a throw occurs.OOP30
                                                                      finally normally executes after try and any selected catch, including when leaving by return or propagating an exception. It is not guaranteed if the process/JVM exits or crashes, or control never leaves the try.OOP31

                                                                      Question 271

                                                                      You catch a general Exception before a specific IOException. What is the result?

                                                                        Source

                                                                        • Object-Oriented Programming review questions · Question 35

                                                                        Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

                                                                        Check the thrown type and catch order before tracing propagation or handler output.

                                                                        Study-guide sections

                                                                        OOP30 · throw, throws and catch selection

                                                                        Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                                        Study-guide references

                                                                        OOP30 · throw, throws and catch selection

                                                                        Answer: Compilation fails because the IOException catch after Exception is unreachable.

                                                                        Exception already catches IOException values because IOException is a subtype. The later subtype handler can never be selected, and OOP30 says this ordering prevents compilation rather than merely causing the general handler to win at runtime. Place the specific IOException catch before Exception if both handlers are needed.

                                                                        Evidence in the complete study note

                                                                        Catch blocks are considered in source order. Place FileNotFoundException before IOException and IOException before Exception; a general catch before a subtype catch makes that later handler unreachable and prevents compilation.OOP30

                                                                        Question 272

                                                                        What does e.printStackTrace() actually print?

                                                                          • Object-Oriented Programming review questions · Question 36

                                                                          OOP31 · finally, cleanup and diagnostic information

                                                                          Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                                          Study-guide references

                                                                          OOP31 · finally, cleanup and diagnostic information

                                                                          Answer: Exception information plus recorded call-stack frames for diagnosis.

                                                                          OOP31 distinguishes getMessage, toString and printStackTrace. The stack trace reports exception information together with recorded call frames, helping locate the call path associated with the failure. It is more diagnostic context than the message alone and does not repair or handle the error by itself. Exact text depends on the exception and recorded frames.

                                                                          getMessage returns the message, toString normally includes type and message, and printStackTrace shows exception information and recorded call frames for diagnosis. Tests should cover expected success, caught failures and propagation. Exception handling does not replace validation or correct an algorithm’s logic automatically.OOP31

                                                                          Question 273

                                                                          Can a finally block change the return value of a try block?

                                                                            Source

                                                                            • Object-Oriented Programming review questions · Question 37

                                                                            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

                                                                            Track pending returns or exceptions and distinguish normal cleanup from process termination.

                                                                            Study-guide sections

                                                                            OOP31 · finally, cleanup and diagnostic information

                                                                            Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                                            Study-guide references

                                                                            OOP31 · finally, cleanup and diagnostic information

                                                                            Answer: Yes. A return from finally overrides the pending try/catch return; avoid it.

                                                                            A try return expression is evaluated before finally runs. A return statement inside finally can replace that pending return and can even suppress an exception, which OOP31 warns against. Merely changing a local after a primitive return expression was evaluated does not automatically recompute that earlier result. The explicit finally return is the clear override mechanism.

                                                                            Evidence in the complete study note

                                                                            A return expression is evaluated before finally; a finally return overrides the pending return and can suppress an exception, so avoid that pattern.OOP31

                                                                            Question 274

                                                                            What is the difference between Error and Exception in Java?

                                                                              Source

                                                                              • Object-Oriented Programming review questions · Question 38

                                                                              Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

                                                                              Separate source errors from runtime exceptions and determine the hierarchy and checked obligation.

                                                                              Study-guide sections

                                                                              OOP29 · Exception hierarchy and checked obligations

                                                                              Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                                              Study-guide references

                                                                              OOP29 · Exception hierarchy and checked obligations

                                                                              Answer: They are Throwable branches: Error usually denotes serious conditions; Exception contains checked and unchecked application exceptions.

                                                                              OOP29 places Error and Exception below Throwable. Error normally signals serious conditions for which routine recovery is inappropriate and its subclasses are unchecked. Exception includes unchecked RuntimeException subclasses and other checked exceptions requiring catch-or-declare handling. It is technically possible to catch Error, so the distinction must not be stated as errors can never be caught.

                                                                              Evidence in the complete study note

                                                                              Throwable is the root of throwable values, with Exception and Error branches. RuntimeException and Error subclasses are unchecked; other throwable classes are checked.OOP29
                                                                              Checked does not mean the exception occurs at compile time: the compiler checks an obligation to catch or declare it, while an actual throw occurs at runtime. A custom exception can extend Exception or RuntimeException. Error normally signals serious conditions for which routine recovery is inappropriate; it is not technically impossible to catch an Error.OOP29

                                                                              Question 275

                                                                              FileNotFoundException is a subclass of IOException. Which catch block executes: catch(IOException e) or catch(FileNotFoundException e)?

If FileNotFoundException is first, that specific block executes. If IOException is placed first with FileNotFoundException afterward, the latter is unreachable and compilation fails. If only IOException is present, it can handle the subclass. The prompt omits order, so these cases must be distinguished.

                                                                                Question 276

                                                                                What does ClassCastException indicate?

                                                                                  Source

                                                                                  • Object-Oriented Programming review questions · Question 40

                                                                                  Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

                                                                                  Separate compile-time cast compatibility from the object’s actual runtime type.

                                                                                  Study-guide sections

                                                                                  OOP21 · Casts and instanceof

                                                                                  Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                                                  Study-guide references

                                                                                  OOP21 · Casts and instanceof

                                                                                  Answer: An attempted reference cast is incompatible with the actual object type.

                                                                                  A cast can be syntactically and type-checkably permitted between related reference types while still fail at runtime. OOP21’s plain Car cannot become a Ferrari merely by casting, so ClassCastException occurs before subsequent method calls. The exception reports an incompatible dynamic type, not object transformation, allocation or a numeric conversion failure.

                                                                                  Evidence in the complete study note

                                                                                  Upcasting a subclass reference to a superclass is implicit and does not change the object. A downcast may pass compile-time type checks yet fail at runtime. Car a=new Car(); Ferrari f=(Ferrari)a; throws ClassCastException before subsequent drive() or brake() calls. It does not turn a plain Car into a Ferrari.OOP21
                                                                                  For Object obj="Hello", (String)obj succeeds and (Integer)obj throws ClassCastException.OOP21

                                                                                  Question 277

                                                                                  Can you use multiple catch blocks for one try block? Can one catch block catch multiple exceptions?

                                                                                    Source

                                                                                    • Object-Oriented Programming review questions · Question 41

                                                                                    Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

                                                                                    Check the thrown type and catch order before tracing propagation or handler output.

                                                                                    Study-guide sections

                                                                                    OOP30 · throw, throws and catch selection

                                                                                    Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                                                    Study-guide references

                                                                                    OOP30 · throw, throws and catch selection

                                                                                    Answer: Yes to both: use ordered catches or a multi-catch such as catch(IOException | SQLException e).

                                                                                    One try can have several catch blocks; source order and specific-before-general reachability still apply. A single multi-catch can also handle alternative exception types. OOP30 prohibits alternatives related by subclassing, so IOException and FileNotFoundException cannot be paired in one union catch. Their hierarchy instead calls for an appropriate common catch or ordered handlers.

                                                                                    Evidence in the complete study note

                                                                                    Catch blocks are considered in source order. Place FileNotFoundException before IOException and IOException before Exception; a general catch before a subtype catch makes that later handler unreachable and prevents compilation. If no catch matches, the exception propagates outward and an uncaught exception terminates its thread. Multiple catch blocks are allowed; catch(IOException | SQLException e) handles alternatives, which must not be related by subclassing.OOP30

                                                                                    Question 278

                                                                                    What is the output? int x = 5; int y = ++x * x--; System.out.println(x + ' ' + y);

                                                                                      Source

                                                                                      • Object-Oriented Programming review questions · Question 42

                                                                                      Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

                                                                                      Track the old and updated values separately and distinguish a character operand from a string.

                                                                                      Study-guide sections

                                                                                      OOP24 · Increment order and the character-space trap

                                                                                      OOP06 · Primitive types, literals and conversions

                                                                                      Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                                                      Study-guide references

                                                                                      OOP24 · Increment order and the character-space trap

                                                                                      OOP06 · Primitive types, literals and conversions

                                                                                      Answer: 73. The expression leaves x=5 and y=36, then adds the space character’s value 32.

                                                                                      Java evaluates ++x first, changing 5 to 6 and supplying 6. x-- then supplies 6 and restores x to 5, so y=36. In x + ' ' + y the space is char, not String, and numeric promotion gives 5+32+36=73. Replacing it with a double-quoted space would instead concatenate separated values.

                                                                                      Evidence in the complete study note

                                                                                      Starting x=5, printing x++ then ++x gives 5 then 7. For int y=++x*x--, Java uses 6*6=36 and leaves x=5. System.out.println(x + ' ' + y) then adds char space’s numeric value 32, so it prints 73. To print separated values, use x + " " + y instead.OOP24
                                                                                      Arithmetic promotes char, byte and short to int in many expressions.OOP06

                                                                                      Question 279

                                                                                      Circle and Sphere are separately declared top-level Java classes. Circle declares private double radius; and Sphere extends Circle. What happens if an instance method of Sphere attempts this.radius = 5.0;?

                                                                                        • Object-Oriented Programming review questions · Question 43

                                                                                        Separate parameters from arguments and operations that read state from operations that change it.

                                                                                        OOP11 · Methods, getters and setters

                                                                                        OOP08 · Access control and package boundaries

                                                                                        OOP16 · this, super, fields and static hiding

                                                                                        Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                                                        Study-guide references

                                                                                        OOP11 · Methods, getters and setters

                                                                                        OOP08 · Access control and package boundaries

                                                                                        OOP16 · this, super, fields and static hiding

                                                                                        Answer: Compilation fails for an ordinary separately declared Sphere: the inherited radius field is private.

                                                                                        The direct field access fails compilation. Circle’s private field is not accessible from a separately declared top-level subclass, and this only identifies the current object; it does not relax visibility. Sphere must use an accessible operation supplied by Circle if it needs to request a radius change. Declaring the classes separately removes the shared-nest exception from the scenario.

                                                                                        Question 280

                                                                                        What is the difference between a concrete class and an abstract class?

                                                                                          Source

                                                                                          • Object-Oriented Programming review questions · Question 44

                                                                                          Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

                                                                                          Check whether a class is concrete and whether every inherited abstract contract has an implementation.

                                                                                          Study-guide sections

                                                                                          OOP18 · Abstract classes and concrete implementations

                                                                                          Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                                                          Study-guide references

                                                                                          OOP18 · Abstract classes and concrete implementations

                                                                                          Answer: A concrete class can be instantiated and must satisfy abstract obligations; an abstract class cannot be directly instantiated.

                                                                                          An abstract class can hold state, constructors, concrete methods and abstract methods, and need not contain an abstract method. A concrete subclass must provide or inherit implementations of every required abstract operation before it can serve as an instantiable class. Abstract is therefore a class-level instantiation/contract restriction, not a prohibition on implemented behavior.

                                                                                          Evidence in the complete study note

                                                                                          An abstract class cannot be directly instantiated but can define fields, constructors, abstract methods and concrete methods. It need not contain an abstract method.OOP18
                                                                                          A concrete subclass must provide or inherit implementations of all required abstract methods; otherwise it must itself be abstract.OOP18

                                                                                          Question 281

                                                                                          String is declared as a final class. What does this mean for developers?

                                                                                            Source

                                                                                            • Object-Oriented Programming review questions · Question 45

                                                                                            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

                                                                                            Decide whether a member belongs to a class or an object, then check initialization and final restrictions.
