                                                                                            OOP07 · Static members, static blocks and final

                                                                                            OOP22 · Identity, equals, toString and immutable strings

                                                                                            Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                                                            Study-guide references

                                                                                            OOP07 · Static members, static blocks and final

                                                                                            OOP22 · Identity, equals, toString and immutable strings

                                                                                            Answer: Developers cannot subclass String; final prohibits extension.

                                                                                            Applying final to String prevents any class from extending String. It does not prevent constructing or referencing String instances, nor does the class modifier alone explain immutability of arbitrary objects. OOP22 treats String’s immutable content as a distinct property. Developers should use existing String operations rather than attempting a String subclass.

                                                                                            Evidence in the complete study note

                                                                                            final prevents reassignment of a variable, overriding of a method or extension of a class. A final reference may still refer to a mutable object.OOP07
                                                                                            Java String objects are immutable. text += " World" assigns a reference to a new concatenated result and can print Hello World without mutating the original String object. final class String prevents subclassing; final alone does not make arbitrary objects immutable.OOP22

                                                                                            Question 282

                                                                                            What is method hiding in Java and how does it differ from overriding?

                                                                                              Source

                                                                                              • Object-Oriented Programming review questions · Question 46

                                                                                              Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

                                                                                              Distinguish the current instance, parent context, hidden fields and static dispatch.

                                                                                              Study-guide sections

                                                                                              OOP16 · this, super, fields and static hiding

                                                                                              OOP15 · Dynamic dispatch: declared type versus actual type

                                                                                              Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                                                              Study-guide references

                                                                                              OOP16 · this, super, fields and static hiding

                                                                                              OOP15 · Dynamic dispatch: declared type versus actual type

                                                                                              Answer: A subclass static method hides a same-signature parent static method; overriding is runtime instance dispatch.

                                                                                              For static hiding, the selected declaration follows the compile-time type used to qualify the call. For eligible overridden instance methods, the object’s runtime class determines the implementation. OOP16’s Animal a=new Dog() static call therefore resolves to Animal, unlike a virtual instance sound call that could invoke Dog. Class qualification makes static selection clearer.

                                                                                              Evidence in the complete study note

                                                                                              Fields are hidden rather than dynamically overridden, and same-signature static methods hide rather than override. With Animal a=new Dog(), a.staticMethod() resolves using Animal’s compile-time type. Prefer Animal.staticMethod() for clarity.OOP16
                                                                                              For Animal a=new Dog(), Animal is the declared type and Dog the actual type. The declared type determines which member operations compile. If fetch() exists only in Dog, a.fetch() fails compilation. For an eligible overridden sound(), a.sound() invokes Dog.sound() at runtime.OOP15

                                                                                              Question 283

                                                                                              Given: interface A { void m1(); } interface B { void m2(); } class C implements A, B {} — What must C define?

                                                                                                Source

                                                                                                • Object-Oriented Programming review questions · Question 47

                                                                                                Identify the interface contract, effective modifiers and permitted implementation forms.

                                                                                                OOP14 · Overriding and restrictions

                                                                                                OOP19 · Interfaces: contracts and modern Java

                                                                                                OOP18 · Abstract classes and concrete implementations

                                                                                                OOP14 · Overriding and restrictions

                                                                                                Answer: C must provide public void m1() and public void m2(), or inherit suitable implementations.

                                                                                                Both unmodified interface declarations are implicitly public abstract. A concrete C implementing A and B must satisfy both signatures, not merely one. In the shown class with no suitable superclass implementation, define public void m1() and public void m2(). Package-private implementations would narrow the public contract; otherwise C must be declared abstract instead of concrete.

                                                                                                A concrete subclass must provide or inherit implementations of all required abstract methods; otherwise it must itself be abstract.OOP18

                                                                                                Question 284

                                                                                                  OOP29 places both Error and Exception under Throwable, establishing the common type for Java throwable values. The distinction between checked and unchecked branches controls catch-or-declare obligations, not whether an exception happens during compilation. Throwable therefore unifies the hierarchy without implying that every subclass is an ordinary recoverable application exception.

                                                                                                    Question 286

                                                                                                    What does 'extensibility' mean in the context of polymorphism?

                                                                                                      Source

                                                                                                      • Object-Oriented Programming review questions · Question 50

                                                                                                      Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

                                                                                                      Check what compiles from the declared type, then select behavior from the actual runtime class.

                                                                                                      Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                                                                      Study-guide references

                                                                                                      OOP15 · Dynamic dispatch: declared type versus actual type

                                                                                                      Answer: New subtypes can supply behavior while existing common-type client code remains reusable.

                                                                                                      OOP15 describes a common Animal array loop invoking speak on Dog and Cat objects. Adding another conforming Animal subtype can supply its own override without rewriting that generic loop. That ability is extensibility through polymorphism: clients depend on the shared contract, while runtime dispatch supplies subtype behavior. The new subtype must still satisfy that contract.

                                                                                                      To solve dispatch questions: check the declaration and visibility, determine the compile-time signature, then identify the object’s runtime class and its most specific override. New subclasses can supply behavior without rewriting this generic loop, which is the practical meaning of extensibility.OOP15

                                                                                                      Question 287

                                                                                                      You have: Object obj = 'Hello'; String s = (String) obj; Is this valid? What about Integer i = (Integer) obj;?

                                                                                                        Source

                                                                                                        • Object-Oriented Programming review questions · Question 51

                                                                                                        Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

                                                                                                        Separate compile-time cast compatibility from the object’s actual runtime type.

                                                                                                        Study-guide sections

                                                                                                        OOP21 · Casts and instanceof

                                                                                                        OOP-S04 · Core package membership and text values

                                                                                                        Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                                                                        Study-guide references

                                                                                                        OOP21 · Casts and instanceof

                                                                                                        OOP-S04 · Core package membership and text values

                                                                                                        Answer: Literal single-quoted Hello is invalid. With "Hello", the String cast succeeds and the Integer cast throws ClassCastException.

                                                                                                        A Java character literal cannot contain the multi-character text 'Hello', so the printed declaration fails before either cast executes. OOP21 explicitly separates that defect from the intended double-quoted version. After changing it to a String literal, obj refers to a String: narrowing back to String succeeds, but narrowing it to Integer fails at runtime.

                                                                                                        Evidence in the complete study note

                                                                                                        For Object obj="Hello", (String)obj succeeds and (Integer)obj throws ClassCastException. A literal 'Hello' is invalid Java syntax; use double quotes for a string literal before tracing the program.OOP21
                                                                                                        A double-quoted string literal denotes a String object. new String(existingString) creates a String with the same text; new String(charArray) copies the array’s characters into an immutable String. A single-quoted literal denotes one char, so several characters enclosed together in single quotes cannot supply a String.OOP-S04

                                                                                                        Question 288

                                                                                                        If a subclass constructor doesn't explicitly call super(), what does Java do?

                                                                                                          Source

                                                                                                          • Object-Oriented Programming review questions · Question 52

                                                                                                          Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

                                                                                                          Trace constructor delegation and initialization in the specified Java version.

                                                                                                          Study-guide sections

                                                                                                          OOP10 · Constructor chaining and initialization order

                                                                                                          Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                                                                          Study-guide references

                                                                                                          OOP10 · Constructor chaining and initialization order

                                                                                                          Answer: If no explicit this(...) or super(...) delegation exists, Java inserts super(); this(...) instead delegates within the class.

                                                                                                          Omitting explicit super() alone is insufficient to determine what happens. A constructor may explicitly call this(...), delegating to another same-class constructor that eventually reaches superclass construction. Only when there is no explicit constructor delegation does OOP10 insert super(), requiring an accessible matching parent no-argument constructor. Otherwise the program fails to compile.

                                                                                                          Evidence in the complete study note

                                                                                                          Under Java 17 rules, an explicit this(args) or super(args) invocation must be the first constructor statement. this invokes another constructor in the same class; super invokes the immediate superclass constructor. A constructor cannot explicitly invoke both. If there is no explicit delegation, an implicit super() is inserted; a matching accessible no-argument parent constructor must exist.OOP10

                                                                                                          Question 289

                                                                                                          What is the difference between a class and an object? Use a concrete example.

                                                                                                            Source

                                                                                                            • Object-Oriented Programming review questions · Question 1

                                                                                                            Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

                                                                                                            Distinguish an object’s stored state, operations, identity and class definition.

                                                                                                            Study-guide sections

                                                                                                            OOP01 · Objects, classes and responsibilities

                                                                                                            Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                                                                            Study-guide references

                                                                                                            OOP01 · Objects, classes and responsibilities

                                                                                                            Answer: A class defines common structure/behavior; an object is one instance, such as a particular Rectangle with width and height.

                                                                                                            Rectangle can define width, height, getArea and getPerimeter for every rectangle. A particular rectangle object stores its own width and height values and responds to those operations. OOP01 distinguishes that instance from the type description: two objects can have equal field values and still have distinct identities. The class is shared structure, not one particular rectangle.

                                                                                                            Evidence in the complete study note

                                                                                                            An object has identity, state and behavior. State is stored in fields; behavior is provided by methods. A Rectangle object may hold width and height and answer getArea() or getPerimeter(). Two objects can have equal fields and still be distinct objects. A class defines their common structure and behavior; an object is a particular instance.OOP01

                                                                                                            Question 290

                                                                                                            Why is encapsulation important? How is it achieved?

                                                                                                              Source

                                                                                                              • Object-Oriented Programming review questions · Question 2

                                                                                                              Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

                                                                                                              Identify whether the emphasis is grouping state, hiding implementation, exposing essentials or varying behavior.

                                                                                                              Study-guide sections

                                                                                                              OOP02 · Four principles and the difference between hiding and abstraction

                                                                                                              OOP11 · Methods, getters and setters

                                                                                                              Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                                                                              Study-guide references

                                                                                                              OOP02 · Four principles and the difference between hiding and abstraction

                                                                                                              OOP11 · Methods, getters and setters

                                                                                                              Answer: Encapsulation protects invariants and stable interfaces by grouping state with validated operations and controlling access.

                                                                                                              OOP02 groups state and operations with controlled access, keeping representation decisions behind stable interfaces. A private account balance exposed through deposit(amount) can reject invalid negative changes rather than permitting unrestricted assignment. This localizes responsibility and lets clients use meaningful operations without depending on internal representation. OOP11 cautions that automatically exposing setters for every field is not required.

                                                                                                              Evidence in the complete study note

                                                                                                              Encapsulation groups related state and operations and controls access. Information hiding keeps implementation decisions behind a stable interface. Abstraction presents the essential operations while omitting details irrelevant to the caller. These ideas overlap: a private balance plus deposit(amount) can demonstrate all three, depending on what the question emphasizes.OOP02
                                                                                                              An accessor/getter returns information; a mutator/setter changes state. Encapsulation does not require blindly generating setters for every field: validate changes and expose only useful operations. For a bank account, deposit must reject negative amounts.OOP11

                                                                                                              Question 291

                                                                                                              What is the difference between method overloading and method overriding? Provide examples.

                                                                                                                Source

                                                                                                                • Object-Oriented Programming review questions · Question 3

                                                                                                                Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

                                                                                                                Compare names and parameter signatures before considering return types or access modifiers.

                                                                                                                Study-guide sections

                                                                                                                OOP12 · Method overloading and compile-time selection

                                                                                                                OOP14 · Overriding and restrictions

                                                                                                                OOP15 · Dynamic dispatch: declared type versus actual type

                                                                                                                Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                                                                                Study-guide references

                                                                                                                OOP12 · Method overloading and compile-time selection

                                                                                                                OOP14 · Overriding and restrictions

                                                                                                                OOP15 · Dynamic dispatch: declared type versus actual type

                                                                                                                Answer: Overloading changes parameter signatures; overriding replaces eligible inherited instance behavior with the same signature.

                                                                                                                For overloading, f(int), f(double) and f(int,int) share a name but have distinct signatures selected using declared arguments at compile time. For overriding, Dog extends Animal and supplies void sound() matching Animal’s eligible void sound(); a superclass reference can then dispatch to Dog at runtime. Changing only the return type cannot create an overload, and override return compatibility still matters.

                                                                                                                Evidence in the complete study note

                                                                                                                Overloaded methods share a name but have different parameter types, counts or type order. Return type alone is insufficient in Java and C++. Overloads can also arise through inherited methods; “same class only” is a teaching simplification. f(int), f(double) and f(int,int) are distinct, but changing a parameter name does not create an overload.OOP12
                                                                                                                The compiler selects the applicable signature from the declared argument types and conversions.OOP12
                                                                                                                A subclass overrides an eligible inherited instance method with the same signature and a compatible return type; a covariant reference return may be a subtype. Visibility cannot become more restrictive, and checked exceptions cannot be broadened incompatibly.OOP14
                                                                                                                For an eligible overridden sound(), a.sound() invokes Dog.sound() at runtime.OOP15

                                                                                                                Question 292

                                                                                                                Why can't Java classes inherit from multiple parent classes? How is this limitation overcome?

                                                                                                                  Source

                                                                                                                  • Object-Oriented Programming review questions · Question 4

                                                                                                                  Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

                                                                                                                  Identify the subtype or ownership relationship and distinguish class inheritance from interface contracts.

                                                                                                                  Study-guide sections

                                                                                                                  OOP13 · Inheritance and useful relationships

                                                                                                                  OOP20 · Conflicting interface methods and abstract class choice

                                                                                                                  Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                                                                                  Study-guide references

                                                                                                                  OOP13 · Inheritance and useful relationships

                                                                                                                  OOP20 · Conflicting interface methods and abstract class choice

                                                                                                                  Answer: Java permits one direct superclass. Use multiple interfaces for type contracts and composition for cooperating implementation/state.

                                                                                                                  The immediate reason the declaration is rejected is Java’s one-direct-superclass rule in OOP13. Multiple interfaces supply multiple type contracts, while contained collaborators model has-a reuse without multiple class inheritance. This does not eliminate every diamond problem: OOP20 requires explicit resolution of conflicting unrelated interface defaults. The note supplies these mechanisms, rather than a historical language-design rationale.

                                                                                                                  Evidence in the complete study note

                                                                                                                  class Dog extends Animal declares a subclass/derived/child of a superclass/base/parent. A class extends one direct class and can implement multiple interfaces. Single, multilevel and hierarchical inheritance mean one parent, a chain, and several children of one parent. Java does not permit class Dog extends Animal,Mammal.OOP13
                                                                                                                  Composition represents has-a, such as Car containing Engine. Reuse alone does not justify an invalid is-a relationship.OOP13
                                                                                                                  Unrelated interfaces providing conflicting defaults require an explicit resolution; interfaces do not remove every diamond ambiguity.OOP20

                                                                                                                  Question 293

                                                                                                                  What is polymorphism? Explain with a code example.

                                                                                                                    Source

                                                                                                                    • Object-Oriented Programming review questions · Question 5

                                                                                                                    Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

                                                                                                                    Check what compiles from the declared type, then select behavior from the actual runtime class.

                                                                                                                    Study-guide sections

                                                                                                                    OOP15 · Dynamic dispatch: declared type versus actual type

                                                                                                                    Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                                                                                    Study-guide references

                                                                                                                    OOP15 · Dynamic dispatch: declared type versus actual type

                                                                                                                    Answer: Polymorphism lets a common-type reference invoke behavior appropriate to the actual subtype.

                                                                                                                    Example: class Animal { void sound() { System.out.println("Animal"); } } class Dog extends Animal { void sound() { System.out.println("Bark"); } } Then Animal a=new Dog(); a.sound(); prints Bark. The declared Animal type makes sound available; the actual Dog object supplies its eligible override at runtime. A new Animal subtype can participate through the same common operation.

                                                                                                                    Evidence in the complete study note

                                                                                                                    For Animal a=new Dog(), Animal is the declared type and Dog the actual type. The declared type determines which member operations compile. If fetch() exists only in Dog, a.fetch() fails compilation. For an eligible overridden sound(), a.sound() invokes Dog.sound() at runtime.OOP15
                                                                                                                    To solve dispatch questions: check the declaration and visibility, determine the compile-time signature, then identify the object’s runtime class and its most specific override. An array Animal[]{new Dog(),new Cat()} can call speak() on each using one loop. New subclasses can supply behavior without rewriting this generic loop, which is the practical meaning of extensibility.OOP15

                                                                                                                    Question 294

                                                                                                                    When would you use an abstract class versus an interface?

                                                                                                                      Source

                                                                                                                      • Object-Oriented Programming review questions · Question 6

                                                                                                                      Hint / Module Reference (Where to Read)

                                                                                                                      Check the kind of inherited method and whether competing contracts require an explicit resolution.

                                                                                                                      Study-guide sections

                                                                                                                      OOP20 · Conflicting interface methods and abstract class choice

                                                                                                                      OOP19 · Interfaces: contracts and modern Java

                                                                                                                      OOP18 · Abstract classes and concrete implementations

                                                                                                                      Answer & Detailed Explanation

                                                                                                                      Study-guide references

                                                                                                                      OOP20 · Conflicting interface methods and abstract class choice

                                                                                                                      OOP19 · Interfaces: contracts and modern Java

                                                                                                                      OOP18 · Abstract classes and concrete implementations

                                                                                                                      Answer: Use an abstract class for shared state/construction/implementation; use an interface for capabilities across unrelated classes and multiple type contracts.

                                                                                                                      An abstract class can centralize common fields, constructor initialization and concrete operations while leaving selected operations abstract. An interface specifies a capability that otherwise unrelated classes can implement, and a class may implement several interfaces. Modern interface defaults do not supply per-instance fields or constructors, so shared object state/construction remains a reason to choose an abstract class.

                                                                                                                      Evidence in the complete study note

                                                                                                                      Use an abstract class for shared state, construction and common implementation; use an interface for a capability across unrelated classes and multiple type inheritance.OOP20
                                                                                                                      No interface instance fields or constructors exist; fields are implicitly public static final.OOP19
                                                                                                                      An abstract class cannot be directly instantiated but can define fields, constructors, abstract methods and concrete methods.OOP18
